preview: Many services use subscriptions, so the way they are designed matters. This story looks at what happens when people decide they no longer want one. Why has ending a subscription become an important consumer issue? By the end, you will understand the main debate behind that question.
comment_1: As you listen, notice what can make canceling a subscription harder than starting one.
comment_2: Part 1 showed that cancelling a subscription can involve extra steps, a kind of friction called sludge. Now, listen for how US regulators tried to address this problem, and what later happened to their rule.
comment_3: This story shows the gap between easy sign-up and difficult cancellation. Next, we will look at the different forms this difficulty can take and why a cancel button is not the whole issue.
comment_4: So, cancellation trouble can take many forms, and the cancel button is only one part of the process. The FTC rule also focused on clear terms and real consent. Now, let’s hear how the article brings these ideas together.
